featured_reviews.name: Hansa Parmar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Stepping into Gaylord feels like travelling back in time with its vintage charm, elegant interiors, and aesthetic ambience. The place has a classic old world vibe and attracts a lovely mix of locals and foreign visitors, making the experience even more special.
We tried the Assorted Vegetable Tandoor Platter, which was flavourful and perfectly grilled. The Mushroom Cheese Lasagna was rich, creamy, and absolutely comforting. To end on a sweet note, the Crème Brûlée was beautifully caramelized and simply delightful.
The food, ambience, and hospitality together make Gaylord a wonderful spot for a relaxed meal at Marine Drive. Highly recommended for those who enjoy timeless charm and delicious food. ❤️✨
⭐ Rating: 5/5 🍽️ Must Try: Assorted Vegetable Tandoor Platter, Mushroom Cheese Lasagna & Crème Brûlée.

featured_reviews.name: Ruchika
featured_reviews.review_text: Absolutely loved the experience here. The interiors are stunning and truly give off elegant British-era vibes — very classy and refined. The ambience feels premium and sophisticated. The coffee was incredibly good and honestly quite addictive! A perfect spot if you’re looking for a high-end, timeless dining experience. ☕✨

featured_reviews.name: Sachin Talwalkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
A 70-year-old iconic establishment of South Bombay, it has long been at the center of fine dining for stars and socialites alike. It was frequently patronized by the likes of Raj Kapoor, Dilip Kumar, and many cricketers. Recently renovated, you step into a regal experience - complete with uniformed waitstaff, European Art Deco accents, and live music.

The menu offers a unique mix of Indian dishes, a few European selections, and non-alcoholic beverages. Unique, because an ambience like this almost demands a glass of wine - something you sorely miss as piano renditions of old and new Bollywood compositions play on.

The food is excellent, the service could be better, but the experience is a must-have. One that transports you back to the charm of old Bombay.

featured_reviews.name: Anannya
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re looking for a place that blends old-school charm with a premium, aesthetic vibe, this is the one. I visited this iconic spot near Marine Lines and honestly, the ambience itself sets the mood. Loved the seating and the service.

What we tried:
Summer Breeze 4.5⭐
Quattro Formaggi  5⭐

The pasta was the highlight as it was runny, rich and sauce. The portion size would be easily filling for two. The mocktail could’ve been sweeter, but still enjoyable.

Make a reservation if you’re planning to go on weekends or during peak dinner hours, it gets busy. Overall, I would rate a 5/5. Definitely going back to explore more on the menu.

featured_reviews.name: Mahesh Maurya
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited this restaurant and found the overall experience to be decent. The food was okay in terms of taste, but it could have been much better if it had been served hot and fresh. Serving lukewarm dishes does affect the dining experience.

On the positive side, the environment and ambiance of the restaurant were quite good—clean, comfortable, and pleasant for dining with friends or family. The staff was polite, and considering the location, the prices are affordable and value for money.

If the restaurant could focus on improving the quality of service, especially ensuring that the food is served hot, it would definitely enhance the overall dining experience.

🥪 Raju Sandwich, Churchgate (Opp. HR College)
One of the go-to spots near Churchgate for a quick and tasty bite. They serve a wide variety of sandwiches, paninis, rolls, and more. The Mexican Panini (4/5 ⭐)is a standout—loaded with flavor, cheesy, and filling (though a bit pricey at around ₹350).
The Chilli Cheese Roll(4/5 ⭐) is another must-try—spicy, gooey, and satisfying.

Their chutneys add a nice zing to everything, and overall, the quality and taste are solid. Tried the Chocolate Sandwich too—it's rich and sweet, but personally found it overwhelming after a few bites (probably better shared). Not a fan of the Pasta Panini—felt too bland for my taste.

Prices are on the higher side for street food, but if you're around HR College or Churchgate and craving something indulgent, it's definitely worth a stop.

featured_reviews.name: Arin Paul
featured_reviews.review_text:
Cafe Bharat, Churchgate, is one of those old-school vegetarian cafés that quietly survives on routine rather than hype. No frills, no experiments, just straightforward food and a steady crowd of office-goers and regulars.

We had Puri Bhaji, Coffee, and Tikki Chole. The puri bhaji was simple and filling, nothing exceptional but nothing to complain about either. The bhaji was mildly spiced, homely in taste, and the puris were fresh enough. The tikki chole was decent; the tikkis were soft and the chole had a familiar North Indian flavour, though it didn’t stand out in any special way. The coffee was basic café-style, served hot, doing its job without trying to impress.

What works in Cafe Bharat’s favour is its budget-friendly pricing, quick service, and convenient location near Churchgate. It’s not a place you’d go out of your way to visit, but if you’re in the area and want a quick, affordable vegetarian meal, it does the job.

The ambience is functional and old-fashioned; clean, but clearly built for efficiency rather than comfort or aesthetics. Service is prompt and no-nonsense.

Overall, Cafe Bharat is reliable, modest, and predictable. Nothing great, nothing bad. Just a simple veg café that knows its role and sticks to it. Suitable for a quick bite, not for culinary excitement.

featured_reviews.name: Sakib Mulla
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Legacy in Transition: Mani’s Cafe, Mumbai…
Mani’s Cafe remains a cornerstone of Mumbai’s South Indian culinary map, yet recent visits suggest it is currently navigating the fine line between its historic "comfort food" status and the pressures of rapid expansion. Whether you’re at the Matunga original or the newer outposts in Chembur and Dadar, the experience is a mix of high-speed efficiency and slightly inconsistent quality.
The Highlights
The Filter Coffee continues to be the undisputed hero—authentic, "kadak," and consistently excellent across branches. The Pineapple Sheera remains a delightful indulgence, and the Thatte Idli offers that fluffy, cloud-like texture that long-time fans crave. If you stick to these classics, the value-for-money remains unbeatable.
The Challenges
The 3-star rating stems from a noticeable inconsistency in their newer fusion offerings. While "Pizza Idli" and "Matka Dosa" sound innovative, they often lean too heavily on mayonnaise and sauces, masking the traditional flavors. Service at the busier QSR outlets (like Matunga East) can feel rushed, and the lack of seating at many locations means you’re often eating in your car or standing in a crowded lane.

featured_reviews.name: Vimall P Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Profoundly Disappointing Culinary Experience

My recent visit to Restaurant Shiv Sagar was, without hyperbole, one of the most profoundly disappointing culinary experiences I have ever endured. This establishment fails catastrophically on every metric that defines a worthwhile restaurant, from the moment you sit down until the moment you thankfully leave. I feel compelled to provide a candid account to ensure fellow diners can make an informed choice and avoid the regret we felt.

The most critical failure lies, undoubtedly, with the food. To simply call it subpar would be a significant understatement; it was, quite frankly, one of the worst meals I have ever consumed. Each dish we ordered was a masterclass in mediocrity, lacking any discernible freshness, flavour, or culinary care. The spices were either absent or jarringly unbalanced, and the overall impression was of food that had been prepared with a sheer lack of interest, tasting bland, pre-made, and carelessly reheated. It was an absolute letdown that formed the core of our negative experience.

This culinary disaster was perfectly complemented by an equally dismal physical environment. The ambiance is best described as poor, with a cramped, cluttered, and uninspiring layout. A significant and frustrating practical issue was the size of the tables. They are inexplicably tiny, making it a genuine struggle to accommodate two plates of food alongside basic essentials like water glasses, condiments, and cutlery. This created a constant, uncomfortable juggling act throughout the meal, completely destroying any possibility of a relaxed dining atmosphere.

To complete this trifecta of failure, the service was exceptionally poor. The staff were inattentive, disinterested, and painfully slow. We waited an eternity to place our order, another eternity for the food to arrive, and a final eternity to receive the bill and settle the payment. Simple requests, like a refill of water, were met with indifference and long delays. The complete absence of basic hospitality was the final straw. In conclusion, Restaurant Shiv Sagar offers no compelling reason for a visit. I cannot recommend it and will unequivocally not be returning.

In terms of value for money, Shiv Sagar offers a satisfying experience. The prices are reasonable, especially considering the generous portions and the quality of the ingredients used. This ensures that you get the most out of your dining experience without breaking the bank.

One of the standout features of Shiv Sagar is its nice variety of dishes. The extensive menu ensures that there is something for everyone, from classic favorites to more unique and innovative creations. This variety keeps the dining experience exciting and caters to diverse palates.

Finally, the great service at Shiv Sagar truly enhances the overall experience. The staff is attentive, courteous, and efficient, ensuring that your needs are well taken care of. Their warm hospitality adds a personal touch that makes you feel valued and welcomed.

In summary, Shiv Sagar is a restaurant that offers a winning combination of good quality food, a convenient location, excellent value for money, a diverse menu, and outstanding service. It's a place where you can enjoy a memorable meal with family and friends.

Cafe Markiv’s feels like a café that knows exactly what it wants to be and stays within that comfort zone. It offers a fairly extensive menu of continental and café-style dishes, presented neatly and priced in the mid-range for the area.

We tried the Americano, Peach Iced Tea, Grilled Chicken Risotto, and Chicken Markiv’s.

The Americano was straightforward and clean, no bitterness, no complexity. It does what an Americano is expected to do, without leaving a strong impression either way. The Peach Iced Tea was refreshing and mildly sweet, pleasant enough for Mumbai weather, though not particularly memorable.

The Chicken Risotto was decent. Creamy, adequately cooked, and comforting, but lacked depth or a distinct flavour punch. It felt safe rather than inspired. A good option if you’re in the mood for something mild and filling, but not something you’d crave or remember later.

The Chicken Markiv’s, which appears to be one of their signature dishes, was served well and plated nicely. The chicken was tender and paired with mashed potatoes and vegetables. Again, the flavours were balanced and acceptable, but it didn’t rise above being just fine. Nothing was wrong with the dish, but nothing truly stood out either.

The menu itself is broad, covering pizzas, burgers, pasta, risottos, rice plates, and main course options, both vegetarian and non-vegetarian. It caters well to mixed groups with varied preferences. Portions are reasonable, and pricing is what you’d expect from a café of this type.

Service was polite and timely, without being overly warm or inattentive. The ambience is comfortable and casual, suitable for conversations, short meetings, or a relaxed meal, though it doesn’t have a distinct character that sets it apart from similar cafés.

Overall, Cafe Markiv’s is reliable but unremarkable. Nothing great, nothing bad. It’s a decent place if you’re nearby and want a predictable café meal without surprises. Not a destination café, but functional and consistent for what it offers.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I’ve visited this branch multiple times, and overall the food quality and service have always been good. The staff is polite and the experience is usually smooth.

However, one major issue I consistently face is the lack of seating. Every time I visit, a large number of people occupy tables for long periods while doing homework, assignments, or working on laptops. While I understand that the environment is comfortable and people enjoy spending time here, it becomes frustrating for customers who actually come to eat.

Today, I saw a person who had just ordered food struggling to find a place to sit, while many tables were occupied by people who had already finished eating or were just sitting and chatting or working. This really shouldn’t be the case.

I believe customers who have ordered food should be given priority for seating. It would be helpful if the on-ground staff could manage this better so that tables are available for diners during peak times.

Overall, a good place but this issue really needs attention.

featured_reviews.name: jayesh singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
A day before my girlfriend and I visited this McDonald’s around 1:30 PM. It was very hot outside and we were already very hungry and feeling dehydrated. The place was a little busy, not too crowded but there were no seats available so we waited around 15 minutes and finally got one.

We kept our bags on the seat and my girlfriend had some important documents inside them. We went to order our food and while ordering I saw one of the staff members taking our bags. I told her those were our bags and we were just ordering food. She put them back but after placing our order and coming back we saw another couple sitting at our table.

After some time I politely said "Excuse me guys this was our seat" and they replied that a staff member removed our bags and gave them the table. I told them we just went to order food. My girlfriend got really frustrated but I controlled the situation. While taking our bags I noticed some important documents had fallen under the seat. Thankfully I saw them in time.

Then we waited again and got another table. Later I went to ask if my order was still preparing because there was no screen showing order numbers. They told me they would call my order number once it was ready. After waiting for a while I asked again and found out my order was already prepared but nobody called me. When I asked about it they simply said "we forgot to call you."

Even the table wasn't cleaned properly. Overall it was a very frustrating experience and the whole thing felt unorganized. I understand places can be busy but handling customers and their belongings like this was really disappointing.

featured_reviews.name: Suraj Jobanputra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Everything was just perfect!

Every single dish we ordered was simply amazing. Here is a breakdown of the highlights:
The Iconic Dosas & Idlis: The Ghee Podi Idli was cloud-soft, drenched in flavorful ghee, and packed a perfect spicy punch with the podi. The Benne Butter Masala Dosa was perfectly crisp on the outside, fluffy on the inside, and rich in flavor.
The Chutneys: A special shoutout to their signature chutneys—fresh, vibrant, and the perfect accompaniment to the main dishes.
The Grand Finale: You cannot leave this place without trying their Coffee Ice Cream. It is an absolute game-changer! It perfectly captures the rich, bold, and aromatic essence of traditional filter coffee but in a creamy, refreshing frozen dessert. It’s not overly sweet, making it the ultimate treat for true coffee lovers.
The service was incredibly fast despite the bustling crowd, and the quality of ingredients truly shines through in every bite.

Verdict: Exceptional food, vibrant vibes, and a 10/10 experience. Whether you are going for a heavy breakfast or a sweet evening treat, this place never disappoints. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Rameshwaram Cafe has been on my list for a while, though I walked in with some hesitation given the mixed reviews online. Glad to say, the experience leaned positive.

We ordered the Benne Pudi Masala Dosa, Benne Masala Dosa, Ghee Pudi Idli, and the Filter Coffee Softy. The dosas arrived crisp, generously buttered, and well-balanced in flavour, while the Ghee Pudi Idli stood out for its richness and depth. The Filter Coffee Softy was an interesting, indulgent twist—worth trying for something different.

What works here is consistency in taste and a certain indulgent South Indian profile that’s clearly designed to appeal to a wider palate. However, the pricing does sit on the higher side for this category, which slightly affects the overall value equation.

I visited on a Monday around 3 PM and was seated in about 30 minutes—manageable by their standards. That said, this isn’t a place I’d personally queue up for on a busy weekend. It’s best experienced when the rush is relatively controlled.

If you’re in that part of the city, it’s definitely worth a visit once—more for the experience than as a regular go-to.

featured_reviews.name: Tarun Joseph
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Rameshwaram Cafe at Churchgate this morning for a quick breakfast like old times.
I’m a Kannadiga and I've lived in Bengaluru for a couple of years and used to visit Rameshwaram Cafe (Indiranagar and JP Nagar outlets), at least once a month. Even now, whenever I go back to Bengaluru, it’s a mandatory stop. So when they announced they were opening in Mumbai, I was genuinely excited. I’ve been missing proper dosa and idli here.

But what I ate today was not Rameshwaram Cafe.

I ordered my usual ghee pudi plain dosa and there was barely any pudi on it. The taste was completely off. It didn’t have the flavour, the texture, or even the smell that makes Rameshwaram Cafe what it is. The taste just felt different, very different. It honestly didn’t even feel like the Rameshwaram Cafe I remember from Bengaluru.
I didn’t try the pudi idli myself, but my friends ordered it and said it was just average as well.

After all the hype, the long queues, and the name they’ve built in Bengaluru, this was unbelievably disappointing. If this is what Rameshwaram Cafe Mumbai is serving, they’re just riding on the Bengaluru brand while delivering something far below that standard.

A truly mediocre experience. If you’ve actually eaten at the Bengaluru outlet, this will feel like a huge downgrade.

featured_reviews.name: Pravin Shinde
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited McDonald's CSMT near Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, and it was a convenient stop in the middle of a busy day in South Mumbai. The outlet is located in a prime area, making it an easy choice for travelers, office workers, and students looking for a quick and reliable meal. Due to its central location, the place is usually crowded, but the system runs smoothly.

The service here is completely self-service. You place your order at the counter or digital kiosk, wait for your token number, and collect your tray once it’s ready. Even during rush hours, the process is quite organized, and the staff handles the crowd efficiently. The waiting time was reasonable, and the order was served fresh.

We ordered a chicken burger combo, cheesy fries, Oreo shake, and a Mc coffee cappuccino. The chicken burger combo was satisfying, with a soft bun and a crispy chicken patty that had the familiar McDonald’s taste. The fries served with the combo were fresh and crispy. The cheesy fries were a highlight, topped with warm, creamy cheese sauce that added extra flavor and made them more indulgent.

The Oreo shake was thick, chilled, and perfectly sweet, making it a refreshing treat. It had a good blend of Oreo flavor and creamy texture. The Mc coffee cappuccino was nicely prepared, with a smooth texture and balanced coffee taste, perfect to relax after a long day.

The taste overall follows their standard franchise model, which means you get consistent flavors just like any other McDonald’s outlet. The seating area is decent, though it can feel a bit crowded during peak hours. Cleanliness is maintained well, and tables are cleared regularly.

Overall, it was a satisfying experience for a quick meal near CSMT. My rating for this outlet is 4 out of 5.

featured_reviews.review_text: Visited Wraps and Rolls on a Wednesday afternoon to grab a quick bite as I was in Colaba. The outlet is small with air-conditioned seating upstairs. featured_reviews.name: Jash Bhavesh Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
We wanted to really try some unique fast foods where there were a variety presented to us and a wide range of options to choose from so we opted for Wraps and Rolls located at Colaba, popularly known as Chikita Cafe. It's a nice cozy place with an open kitchen and a great seating place along with it.
We tried a variety of dishes ranging from starters to beverages and we weren't disappointed at all.
I'll walk y'all through my honest experience with this place.
▪︎For starters :
• Onion Rings
The popular British invention which dates back at least 200 years. Fried Onion rings sprinkled with chat masala and other spices.
• Grande Nachos
This place serves actually unique nachos. They don't have the standard corn nacho chips, but have cheese flavored, Jalepeno flavored and beetroot flavored nacho chips. When served with salsa and nacho cheese, this beats all the nachos you've had till date.
• Cheese Garlic Bread
An all timer in cheesy garlic bread, the aromatic appetizer always finds place in my appetite
▪︎Mains:
Paneer Tikka Roll
Medium Spicy, Paneer Tikka cooked in tandoor with mint chutney and lacha onions.
▪︎Beverages
• Chocolate Milkshake
This amazing, amazing Chocolate milkshake had an unmatched aroma, freshly crushed chocolate and considerable Hershey's syrup
• Mint Mojito
Diced mint and kind of fizzy, this tonic based mocktail should be on your list.

So overall, I loved the experience. It was a pretty solid experience and the caretaker/manager both were prettyhelpful with what to choose and what not to choose .
So overall
Taste: 5/5
Quantity: 5/5
Menu Varieties: 4.5/5
Quality: 4.5/5
Overall: 9.8/10 ❤️
